site.name: orbitride
site.summary: orbitride-clone Fictional intercity rideshare / bus booking flow "OrbitRide". Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Landing: search box (From / To city autocomplete datalist, date, passengers) + 3 value props + 6 popular-route cards | | `routes.html` | Trip results list: left filters (time-of-day, price slider, 4 amenities multi-select); top 7-day date carousel; 8 trip rows (carrier, departure–arrival, duration, stops, amenities, seats left, price, Select button) | | `seats.html` | SVG bus seat map: front 2 priority rows, middle 11 standard 2+2 rows, rear 5-seat row; selectable count = passengers; occupied / selected / standard / priority states; right side legend + selected list + price box + Continue |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full orbitride system, prioritizing the primary checkout/booking flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The OrbitRide checkout flow successfully demonstrates state persistence and dynamic pricing across its desktop and mobile pages. However, severe accessibility blockers prevent keyboard and screen reader users from progressing past the seat selection and passenger details steps. Additionally, mobile users face critical usability issues, including horizontal overflow that hides primary actions, and a broken payment form that silently fails to provide validation feedback.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively evaluate the OrbitRide booking flow from initial search to confirmation, with a strong emphasis on cross-page state persistence (passenger count, total price) and mobile usability.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start on the landing page to test the search inputs, paying special attention to the datalist autocomplete and date pickers. It will then navigate to the routes page to test filtering logic, proceed to the SVG seat map to validate seat selection rules based on passenger count, and finish by passing through the passenger details, extras, and payment pages to verify the checkout flow.
assumptions: The booking flow strictly follows the sequence: index -> routes -> seats -> passengers -> extras -> payment -> confirmation.
The passenger count selected on index.html dictates the number of seats required on seats.html and the number of forms on passengers.html.
The mock data supports generic city names or specific autocomplete options for the Midwest.
risk_hotspots: From/To city autocomplete behavior across browsers and viewports.
Mobile layout and usability of the left-hand filter sidebar on routes.html.
SVG interactive seat map on seats.html (checking selection limits matching passenger count).
Top navigation links (OrbitRide, Routes, Help, Sign in) failing mobile tap target sizing (currently ~21px height).

phases.title: Search and Landing Setup
phases.objective: Verify the search widget inputs, datalist interactions, and mobile navigation.
key_checks: Type partial city names into FROM/TO to trigger autocomplete.
Set PASSENGERS to a value > 1 to track it later.
Attempt to submit an empty form to check validation.
Verify top navigation links on mobile viewport.
exit_criteria: Successfully filled the search form and navigated to routes.html.

phases.title: Routes and Filtering
phases.objective: Ensure the routes page accurately updates based on filters and displays correctly on mobile.
key_checks: Toggle 'Departure time' select, 'Max price' slider, and 'Amenities' checkboxes.
Verify that the route list updates or behaves correctly with filters.
Click a 'Select' button for a specific trip.
exit_criteria: Filters have been interacted with and the user has successfully navigated to seats.html.

phases.title: Seat Selection Logic
phases.objective: Validate the SVG seat map interactions and passenger count enforcement.
key_checks: Attempt to select more seats than the passenger count.
Attempt to proceed with fewer seats than the passenger count.
Interact with different seat types (priority vs standard) to see price updates.
exit_criteria: Successfully selected the exact number of required seats and progressed to passengers.html.

phases.title: Checkout Flow Completion
phases.objective: Walk through passenger details, extras, and payment to reach confirmation.
key_checks: Verify the number of passenger forms matches the initial count.
Add an extra (e.g., baggage) and check if the total price updates.
Complete payment form with mock data.
Verify final confirmation details reflect the choices.
exit_criteria: Reached confirmation.html with no blocking errors.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 7 HTML pages defined in the site structure.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise search autocomplete, route filters, SVG seat selection, and dynamic pricing.
coverage_targets.mobile: Evaluate navigation tap targets, filter sidebar layout, and SVG seat map scaling.

notes: Since this is a fictional clone, expect local storage or URL parameters to pass state between pages rather than a backend database.

findings.problem: The interactive SVG seat map elements lack semantic HTML tags, ARIA roles, and keyboard focusability (`tabindex`).
findings.evidence: Trajectory chunks note: 'The SVG seat map elements are not recognized as interactable in the accessibility tree... making them inaccessible to keyboard.'
findings.why_it_matters: Keyboard-only and screen reader users cannot interact with the seat map, completely blocking them from selecting seats and completing the checkout flow.
findings.suggestion: Add `role="button"`, `tabindex="0"`, and keyboard event listeners (e.g., Space/Enter to select) to the SVG `<rect>` or `<path>` elements representing the seats.

findings.user_goal: Compare routes and select a trip on a mobile device
findings.problem: The routes page fails to adapt to mobile screens, causing severe horizontal overflow that pushes critical ride details and call-to-action buttons off-screen.
findings.evidence: A horizontal overflow layout warning indicates a 760px page width on a 390px viewport. The agent noted that 'essential ride details and the Select buttons are pushed out of the initial viewport'.
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users must discover they need to scroll horizontally to see the 'Select' button, causing high friction and likely leading to significant drop-off at the top of the funnel.
findings.suggestion: Implement responsive CSS media queries to stack the filter sidebar above the results list and ensure route cards adapt to 100% of the viewport width.

findings.user_goal: Submit payment details and be notified if required information is missing
findings.problem: The payment inputs are not wrapped in a `<form>` tag, which breaks native HTML5 validation, and no custom inline error messages are provided for empty fields.
findings.evidence: When clicking 'Pay' with empty fields on mobile, the action failed silently. The agent noted: 'DOM lacks a <form> tag, which prevents native HTML5 required field validation from functioning.'
findings.why_it_matters: If a user forgets a field and clicks 'Pay', nothing happens and no feedback is given. Users will not know what to fix, leading to confusion and abandoned purchases.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the payment inputs in a standard `<form>` element, ensure `required` attributes are set, and implement visible inline error messages (e.g., red borders and text) when validation fails.

findings.user_goal: Enter details for a second passenger using keyboard navigation
findings.problem: The form fields for additional passengers (Passenger 2) are missing from the programmatic accessibility tree and cannot be reached via keyboard Tab navigation.
findings.evidence: In the passenger flow, pressing Tab reached Passenger 1's fields, but 'Passenger 2's First name, Last name, Date of birth... inputs are completely missing from the interactables list.'
findings.why_it_matters: Assistive technology users are completely prevented from booking tickets for more than one person because they cannot focus or fill out the subsequent passenger forms.
findings.suggestion: Check for duplicate HTML `id` attributes on the generated Passenger 2 inputs, ensuring every input has a unique `id` and a properly linked `<label for="...">`.

findings.user_goal: Select an alternative payment method (e.g., Apple Pay)
findings.problem: Selecting 'PayLite' or 'Apple-Pay-like' radio buttons does not dynamically hide the credit card specific input fields.
findings.evidence: The agent selected 'Apple-Pay-like' on mobile and observed: 'successfully highlights the option, but fails to hide the credit card specific input fields (Cardholder name, Card number, etc.)'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users selecting an alternative payment method may be confused, wondering if they are still required to manually enter their credit card details in addition to using Apple Pay.
findings.suggestion: Dynamically hide or disable the credit card specific inputs (Name, Number, Expiry, CVC, Zip) when a non-card payment method is selected.

findings.user_goal: Opt into saving account details during payment
findings.problem: The 'Save to my OrbitRide account' checkbox is severely disconnected from its text label.
findings.evidence: Recent trajectory screenshots show the checkbox input centered under the CVC field, while the label text is pushed far to the right edge under the Apply button.
findings.why_it_matters: The extreme visual gap violates the law of proximity, making it difficult for users to immediately associate the checkbox with the action it performs.
findings.suggestion: Group the checkbox input and its `<label>` within a flexbox container (`display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px;`) to ensure they stay visually attached across all viewports.
findings.source_hint: payment.html: Save to my OrbitRide account

findings.user_goal: Quickly add multiple pieces of luggage
findings.problem: The luggage quantity input fields are strictly `readonly`, forcing users to rely entirely on tiny +/- stepper buttons to change values.
findings.evidence: The agent attempted to type '2' into the input but failed because 'element is not editable'. The adjacent +/- buttons triggered small tap target warnings (28x28px).
findings.why_it_matters: Forcing users to repeatedly tap very small controls (28x28px) creates interaction friction, particularly on mobile devices or for users with motor impairments.
findings.suggestion: Remove the `readonly` attribute to allow direct numeric typing (e.g., `type="number"`), and increase the dimensions of the +/- stepper buttons to meet the 44x44px mobile touch target minimum.

gaps: 2 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
